To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the TnT mutations that cause familial cardiomyopathy and sudden cardiac death have differential effects on the inotropic response of mouse hearts to increased myofilament calcium sensitivity.
the inotropic responsiveness to isoproterenole and exercise is impaired in transgenic mice expressing a TnT mutation that causes a high rate sudden cardiac death in humans.
the inotropic response of hearts expressing the TnT‐79I mutant (TnT‐I) was impaired, whereas hearts expressing the T79C mutant (TnTC) were not different from controls.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of the heart failure and the development of novel therapeutic approaches.
the role of Ca2+‐dependent and Ca2+‐independent mechanisms in the regulation of the contractility of the heart muscle.
the role of the myofilament Ca(2+) sensitivity increase in the pathogenesis of FHC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Ca2+ sensitizing effects of TNNI3 mutations may reduce the inotropism of the mouse heart to catecholamines, and that this effect is more pronounced for mutations that also affect diastolic function, such as TNNI3-I79N.
the I79N mutant has a more severe impact on contractility than the R278C mutant and the effect of the R278C mutation is similar to the effect of the wild‐type TNNI3 gene.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TnT‐mediated Ca2+ sensitization is not sufficient to cause FHC in mice, but it may contribute to a more malignant phenotype in humans.
TnT‐mediated Ca2+ sensitivity is a key determinant of cardiac contractility.
the I79N mutant has a more severe effect on the inotropic state than the R278C mutant.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Ca2+ sensitivity‐enhancing effects of TnI mutations may reduce the contractile responsiveness of mouse hearts.

the Ca2+ sensitizing effect of TnT‐related FHC mutations is a double‐edged sword: on one hand it contributes to the development of hypertrophy and diastolic dysfunction, but on the other hand it reduces the ability of the heart to respond to increased inotropic stimuli.
TnT mutations that cause hypertrophic cardiomyopthy and sudden cardiac death have a differential effect on cardiac function, depending on their ability to increase myofilament calcium sensitivity.
